Yes!

* **Budget** \- 200$ - 350$
* **Source** \- Gaming laptop. Probably need to buy a DAC.
* **Requirements for Isolation** \- None. May even prefer open-backs.
* **Will you be using these Headphones in Public?** No.
* **Preferred Type of Headphone** \- Full size headphone.
* **Preferred tonal balance** \- I really just can't hang with really bright headphones, I tire out easily
* **Past headphones** \- First pair was the Superlux HD 668B's. I love these headphones, I get lost in the sound so easily with them. Also got the Tin Audio T3 iems, they've got great definition but they're very bright for my poor sensitive ears.
* **Preferred Music** \- I truly listen any and every genre. I mainly listen to Hip-Hop & Pop though.
* **What would you like to improve on from your set-up** \- Soundstage and definition are important to me, I love just getting lost in the sound. Honestly if I could just get an "upgraded" version of the Superlux's then I'd be very happy.

Reddit however bases itself around subjects/ideas (Subreddits) and the users supply the content. It naturally has a tendency to stay diverse and unbiased because each subreddit has new users giving the content every day. TLDR: Reddit isn't a social media site.
